items.title: Robots now perform 2 of every 3 knee replacements, Stryker CEO says
items.summary:
Stryker builds every one of its orthopedic surgery robots in the U.S. CEO Kevin Lobo says it will stay that way, because of what’s happening in China.

“We have no plans to make any robots in China. The IP is a massive worry,” Lobo said Monday at the F500 Innovation Forum in Detroit. “They are knocking off a lot of the other robots.”

Robots are now central to how Stryker sells joint replacements. Lobo said two of every three Stryker knee replacements are now done robotically, using its Mako system, which has been used in 2.5 million procedures in 47 countries.
